sections.text: Teachers, fathers, sons and also grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives,-
These I do not wish to kill, though they kill me, O Krishna, even for the sake of dominion over the three worlds; leave alone killing them for the sake of the earth.
By killing these sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure can be ours, O Janardana? Only sin will accrue to us from killing these felons.

Dhritarashtra asked the question: Whats happening in Dharmakshetra Kurukshetra, and what are my sons and Pandavas doing? From Duryodhanas perspective, he was insecure. Even though he had the largest army, he could not take winning for granted. Then we saw Arjunas request to Krishna to put the chariot in the middle of the army.
And once Krishna did that, Krishna simply said: Look at Bheeshma, Drona, all the Kauravas gathered here, ready to fight. Most of the time, we focus on what we are trying to achieve in life. And then when we achieve it, we take all the credit ourselves.
We tend to forget that lots of people have to make lots of sacrifices for us to get to that point. Basically, Krishnas message to Arjuna is: Look at how many people are here to support your cause. Make sure you acknowledge that, its not you alone who will be capable of winning this war.
Arjuna always thought he could win this war. He has won it before. You know, he went to fight with Drupada for Drona and earned half his kingdom for Drona.
He fought with Gandharvas when they captured Duryodhana. And he also fought Kauravas army when they attacked Viratas kingdom. And he has won all the time.
He has not learned yet what failure is in his life. So he had his own opinion about what his capabilities are and what he can do. But when he sees both sides, he sees the enormity of the task.
That is not as simple as just winning the battle against enemies. Now you are fighting among your own people, in the people who are as capable of himself, Bheeshma and Drona and all other people, Karna and. And he sees that on his side also all his family members are there to help him.
That creates confusion in his mind. So we have seen last few verses that he first had this nervous breakdown. What am I doing here? Is this the right thing to do? Is it really worth fighting this war.
And finally he has the delusion about what the situation is all about. So then he obviously starts describing what hes feeling. So first he said, I cant even stand my body shivering.
I cant even hold my Gandiva. The Gandiva is slipping away from my hand. All the physical symptoms of person who is having nervous breakdown.
But now hes describing what he thinks the reality is a delusion. Person sees reality as if hes seeing in a dream, an alternate reality. Other people see reality one way but the person is under delusion.
He sees reality differently. He starts describing his reality very differently. The first thing he says, Nimitta ni che pasyami vi paritha ni keshava nacha shreyo anupashyami hatva sajanam ahave.
Nothing good is going to come out of this war. I now see that something wrong is happening here. So we can see now he is having a superstition.
My left eye is fluttering. So thats not good, right? I had a surgery on Thursday. We were getting ready and Meena was boiling milk.
Now obviously you know what we consider bad omen? So Mina was very careful. She was standing right in front of the milk and I didnt even know any of that. But Im just sitting there.
And then for one second she turned around to, to wash a cup or something and the milk spilled and she literally screamed, you know, I dont. I said, what happened? I thought that something really bad had really happened. So I got up from the chair and said, whats happened? Thats just the milk.
I thought, oh, thats okay. I didnt want this to happen. So I realized inside whats bothering her because we were already double minded going for a surgery because my vision was relatively okay.
But doctor said your lens has come loose and it can fall anytime. So its good to get it done. I say you can do it whenever you feel like, but its not going anywhere.
But still, like your camera lens is loose. We decided, well, lets get it over with. And I realized what is bothering her, that we are going for surgery and hes a bad omen.
So I didnt say a word because I knew what she was bothering her. But I didnt discuss that because I knew if I discuss that, it will go even further back if I try to say, dont worry, I dont believe in that. Lets even make it worse.
I have not Discussed that with her. But I could see clearly what she was worried about. So whenever mind is not seeing the reality clear, then its a simple milk boiling over.
It works as described in physics books. But we dont see it that way. Its not the laws of physics now we are worried about.
Were worried about some metaphysical rules of how things work in this world. So Arjuna now is not seeing reality as is. He said, Im not seeing.
I think logically I come to this country simply. I just see bad omens. So thats the sign of a delusion.
And then he says, Nakank se Vijayam Krishna Nacharajyam Sukha nicha kim no Rajya na Govinda kim bhogi jeevte Nava. I desire no victory, O Krishna. I dont own the kingdom Na Sukhani.
I dont any comforts. What is the purpose of having all this domain to us? Govinda Isham arthe kanksitam nah Rajyam Bhogaha Sukha nicha ta IME Avasthita Yudhte pranam tyaktva Dhananicha. For whom we desire this kingdom and comforts for our own people.
Every parent says that we have done this for our children. Nobody said I did it for myself. This is for whom we desire this kingdom and this comfort and all the prosperity.
They are standing here to fight this war. Acharyaha, Pitaraha, Putraha, Tatha, Ivach, Pita Mah. My teachers, my fatherly relatives.
Matulaha, Swasuraha, Pautraha, Shyalaha, Samandinisthada. My sons, grandfathers, maternal relatives, Swasuraha in laws, Potraha. My grandchildren, Sialaha in laws again, Sabandin and all other relatives.
Etan ichami Gnatoapi Madhusudana. I do not desire to kill them. Even if I get killed, Even if I get the domain over all three worlds.
Some of Puranas describe three worlds. Swargalok, Mrityulok and Patal Lok Mrityulog. Because we are all mortals, things are impermanent.
In Mrityulog, Swargalok, everything is always pristine and serene. Patalok is beyond our world. More like past, present and future.
So even if I have the domain of all three worlds, its not worth it to kill my own people. Then what is the point in fighting for a little piece of Land, this little kingdom on this earth, in this mortal world. So he made his statement very clear.
Now, if these words were his own, after reflection on the situation over a period of time and very intense contemplation, whether this is right or thats right, then he comes to this conclusion. These are very noble words for whom we are desiring all this. If these people are not going to benefit, or these people have to make sacrifice, its not worth it.
But we know that he did not do that before, because just before Bheeshma Parva, theres Udayoga Parva. Bheesma Parva starts when the war starts. The efforts both sides made to avoid this war.
Drupada sends his Brahmin diplomat to go and negotiate it out. Look, this war is not worth. So Drupadas emissary goes to Dhritarashtras court and makes the argument why it is best for everybody to divide this kingdom into half as it was before, give Pandavas theirs.
This enough for both of you to enjoy these kingdoms. Dhritarashtra was pretty much convinced that thats the right thing to do. Bhishma had given his advice that to avoid this war, this is the only way.
Karna interrupted Bhma and said no. Yudhishthira lost his kingdom in this game of dice. Now if he wants this kingdom back, he has to beg.
There is no settlement. And Visma actually told Karna that if you dont listen to what the guy just say and dont agree to it, youll end up in a war. And thats not going to be any good for anybody.
So there are two characters here who are against settlement, Duryodhana and Karna. Karna had his own agenda. He had no interest in who wins this war.
You know, his agenda was he wanted to prove hes better than Arjuna. If this war does not occur, Karna had no chance to prove that he is better than Arjuna. So he has his own agenda.
So then I can prove myself that Arjuna is not the best archer in the world. I am the best archer in the world. Then Dhritarashtra sends Sanjaya to Yudhishthira to have his side of proposal for settlement.
And that proposal was very simple. War is not good for anybody. Exactly the words which you are hearing from Arjuna.
So Sanjaya made his case. Im here on behalf of King Dhritarashtra. King is reminding you that my children are spoiled.
They are not listening to me. What they are doing is not right. However, you people are good people.
You should know what is right and wrong. Its like two children fighting in a family. You also dont understand being an older one.
Exact same message to the Yudhishthira that you are. Dharmaraj, how can you engage in this Adharma of fighting a war against your own cousins? Arjun at the time said give Duryodhan a message that Keshav and I will kill you, the evil Dury and all evil cousins. Even Indras army cannot defeat when Krishna and I are together.
And he said my Gandiva is twitching, arrows are peeping out of cleaver. So he basically said Im so anxious. But Dhritarashtra plants the seeds that the war is never good.
The result of any war is nothing but hell whether you win the war or lose the war. So the ideas presented were logical. When you look at it from a very narrow perspective.
So here the words which are hearing from Arjuna are literally borrowed from Sanjayas message, then there is no good coming out of it. This is a case of a rift between your Buddhi and your mind. Buddhi is your subjective mind.
This buddhi is available when Im thinking very rationally and seeking Buddhist guidance. Hes already demonstrated that he lost all control over his mind. So this subjective mind, which is buddhi, an objective mind, objective mind is simply receiving information from outside and trying to interpret.
But it does not have much experience. So it has to rely on a Buddha to decide whether this situation is what it is all about and how to react to the situation. So here Arjuna is now one side.
He is torn between his desire to win over Duryodhana, set the record straight and get what is rightful his because hes capable of doing so. The other side, he now remembers that everything Sanjaya said is true. Theyre all standing right in front of me and I have to fight them and I have to kill them.
They may get killed, my people may get killed. But in the end the winning or losing may not mean anything because we have lost our own people. So right now what we are seeing is confusion created by Dhritarashtra.
Like the argument we hear recently in our impeachment. Some Republican senators or congressmen said whatever Trump did is not right, but it is not worth impeaching. We should be sorting this out internally.
Dhritarasa sent the same message through Sanjaya. Whatever Duryodhana is doing is not right. But if you people are wise enough.

In verse 34, Arjuna catalogs his relationships across the battlefield: Acharyas (teachers), pitarah (fathers), putras (sons), pitamahas (grandfathers), matulas (maternal uncles), shvashuras (fathers-in-law), pautras (grandsons), shyalas (brothers-in-law), sambandhinas (relatives). This exhaustive list reveals that Arjuna is now drowning in a sea of relationships, unable to see anything else, not the thirteen years of exile, not Draupadis humiliation, not the multiple assassination attempts by the Kauravas.
Verse 35 contains a revealing phrase: Api trailokya rajyasya hetoh, even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, I would not kill them. Then he adds: Kim nu mahikrite, let alone for this earthly kingdom. Notice how he escalates to cosmic proportions. This is the mind in distress, constructing ever-grander justifications.
But verse 36 reveals the deepest confusion: Nihatya dhartarashtran nah ka pritih syat, what pleasure can we have by killing Dhritarashtras sons? And then: Papam eva ashrayed asman hatva etan atatayinah, sin alone would accrue even though they are felons (atatayinah). Arjuna acknowledges that his enemies ARE felons deserving punishment under dharma-shastra, yet concludes that punishing them would still be sinful. This is the rift between buddhi and manas, knowing whats right yet feeling pulled toward inaction. Reflect on situations where youve acknowledged someones wrongdoing yet felt paralyzed about addressing it. Yes, they violated my trust, but theyre family. Yes, this is harmful, but taking action seems worse. The Gita will teach us to see through such confusion, but first we must recognize it within ourselves.
